LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 1.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND LISTENING COMPREHENSION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five
Subject: General
Strand: CHILD RIGHTS AND RESPONSIBILITIES Suggested Vocabulary: responsible, food, cloth
Topic 1.1: Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension, part of CHILD RIGHTS AND RESPONSIBILITIES Suggested Vocabulary: responsible, food, cloth in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five General.

Key inquiry question: Why should we say the sounds in words, phrases, and sentences correctly? 2. How can we improve our pronunciation? 3. Why should we listen attentively?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Responsibility is inculcated as the learner learns about child rights and responsibilities and practises them while making an

audio recording of a poem containing the target sounds and playing the audio for effective feedback.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life Skills: Effective communication is achieved as the learner articulates the target sounds clearly and also listen to audio of

the target sound.

Link to other Subjects:

The learner can link the content of child rights when they learn about child rights and responsibilities in Social Studies.
